task: Oracle dialect: support the optional `WHERE` clause on the `UPDATE` and `INSERT` branches of a `MERGE` statement (`WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ... WHERE ...`, `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT ... VALUES ... WHERE ...`), so it parses and round-trips in Oracle. When transpiling to dialects that do not support it, emit an unsupported warning and drop the clause.
why: Both make the same parser change and both pass. Both add a dialect flag that only Oracle turns on, and both emit an unsupported warning and drop the clause when it is off. So scope and correctness are equal. The tie broke on fidelity and minimality. c1 checks for the `WHERE` arg up front and never generates SQL it is going to throw away. Its test uses `helper_logger`, the pattern existing tests already use (`test_transpile.py`, `test_bigquery.py`). c2 always renders the `WHERE` SQL first and only then discards it. Any warnings raised while rendering that dropped condition would still be recorded. It also repeats the `where = ...` line in both branches. c2's flag name (`SUPPORTS_MERGE_WHEN_WHERE`) does follow the more common `SUPPORTS_*` naming, but that edge doesn't outweigh the above.
